doc.title: Rob Mounsey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 9, 2025

title: Record producers, and Russ Titelman's ear
summary: Jokes about producers who don't know what they want, and an anecdote of Russ Titelman asking him to drop the 13th from a chord.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah. As a producer yourself, sometimes I wonder if you have trouble zipping your mouth in a session because like you know that something should be done differently but it’s not your role to say that?
Well if I’m producing a record it is my role to say that. I mean it’s like being the director of a movie. If I’m the producer and I think —

Yeah. Yeah. Well you know there are all kinds of producers. There’s no licensing for that job. So some are really very, very knowledgeable, competent and know what they want; and many others are, you know, famously — the jokes about record producers are that they don’t know what they want and they’re just kind of flailing and hoping something happens. You know?
Because they’ll take credit for it.
Well sure. “How many record producers does it take to change a light bulb?” “I don’t know, what do you think” is the joke.
But they’re not all like that and I have to say my friend Russ Titelman is not whatsoever like that. I’ve done a lot of stuff with him, you’re familiar with that name maybe.

He’s an old friend of mine and he’s the only guy who could ever do something like I was playing a chord as a synthesizer overdub, and it was a little bit of a thick sort of jazz- adjacent kind of chord with a lot of notes in it. And he walked up to my left ear and he said, “What’s that note [hums a pitch].” He very softly sings a note [hums] and yes it is in the chord I’m playing. And I say, “Oh that’s the G natural, it’s the — it’s actually the 13th. He says, “We don’t need that note.” And he was right. And I didn’t play that note. He was exactly right. We didn’t need that — and I was pretty impressed by that. But he was a musician. He doesn’t really play now I think but that he should hear a note in the chord and tell me to take out the most sophisticated note because it wasn’t appropriate. I don’t know anyone else that could do that actually.
